# EBIKE101 Day 2: Bicycle Mechanics Foundations

## Official focus

Students prove the conventional bicycle is mechanically safe before adding electrical complexity. The lesson covers bicycle anatomy, the ABC quick check, tire and wheel condition, braking, steering, drivetrain condition, fastener awareness, and repair documentation.

## Today's big question

What must a normal bicycle prove before it is worthy of electric assist?

## Core rule

Electricity does not repair a loose wheel, weak brake, damaged tire, or unstable steering system.

## Learning targets

Students will be able to:

1. Identify the frame, fork, headset, stem, handlebars, wheels, tires, brakes, drivetrain, pedals, cranks, saddle, and seatpost.
2. Complete an air, brakes, chain/crank, and quick-release or axle check.
3. Recognize rubbing, looseness, damage, poor adjustment, and unsafe routing.
4. Perform one instructor-approved basic maintenance action.
5. Record the complaint, inspection, action, and verification in a repair log.

## Materials and staging

- One conventional bike or e-bike per team when available
- Bike stands when available
- Tire pump and pressure gauge
- Hex keys, open-end wrenches, tire levers, clean rags, and chain lubricant
- Eye protection and gloves as appropriate
- Repair tags and student packets
- No battery power during mechanical work

## Five-hour run of show

| Time | Block | Instructor move |
|---|---|---|
| 10:00-10:10 | Landing | Attendance and Day 1 review: power comes after control. |
| 10:10-10:30 | Morning quiz | Check safety thinking and bicycle vocabulary. |
| 10:30-11:00 | Bike anatomy | Walk the bike from front contact patch to rear contact patch. |
| 11:00-11:30 | ABC quick check | Air, brakes, chain/crank, steering, wheels, and contact points. |
| 11:30-12:00 | Demo | Model one repair log: complaint, evidence, action, verification. |
| 12:00-12:30 | Lunch/reset | Bikes stable, tools returned, batteries off. |
| 12:30-1:10 | Lab A | Team mechanical inspection and anatomy worksheet. |
| 1:10-1:50 | Lab B | One instructor-approved maintenance action per team. |
| 1:50-2:05 | Break | Reset tools and keep bikes stable. |
| 2:05-2:35 | Lab C | Recheck and document the result. |
| 2:35-2:55 | Debrief | What changed, what evidence proves it, and what remains unsafe? |
| 2:55-3:00 | Close | Preview Day 3 control and power paths. |

## Stop-work triggers

- Unstable bike or unsafe stand setup
- Battery left on during mechanical service
- Unknown wheel or axle retention
- Brake cable, hose, pad, rotor, or rim damage beyond the approved task
- Cracked frame or fork, damaged tire casing, loose steering, or missing fastener
- Student attempts to ride before instructor approval
- Tool use that could damage a component or injure someone

## Afternoon lab

Teams complete a front-to-back anatomy check, an ABC quick check, and a repair log. Each team may complete one approved action such as correcting tire pressure, tightening an accessible non-critical accessory, cleaning and lightly lubricating a chain, or correcting obvious cable routing. Brake, steering, wheel-retention, or structural work stays instructor-controlled unless specifically demonstrated and approved.

## Student artifact

Bike anatomy worksheet plus repair log containing:

1. Complaint or observed condition
2. Evidence found
3. Approved action
4. Verification after the action
5. Remaining concern or instructor review item

## Completion standard

Students can explain that a powered bicycle is still a bicycle first, identify the main mechanical systems, complete a repeatable check, and document what was actually verified.

## Backup plan

If bikes or stands are limited, rotate teams through one instructor demonstration bike while other teams complete a photo-free paper anatomy map, inspection sequence, and repair-log scenario.

## Morning quiz answer sequence

1 B, 2 A, 3 C, 4 B, 5 C, 6 B, 7 B, 8 C, 9 B, 10 C, 11 B, 12 C, 13 B, 14 B, 15 C, 16 B, 17 C, 18 B, 19 C, 20 B.

## Google Classroom post

Today we focus on the bicycle underneath the electrical system. Complete the morning quiz, anatomy worksheet, ABC quick check, one instructor-approved maintenance action, and repair log. Turn in the completed student packet. Success means you can name what you checked, what evidence you found, what you changed, and how you verified it.
